quest.title: Life on the High Seas
quest.description: At Beidou's invitation, you take part in the "Shield of the Crux" sailor training. Time to get a taste of life out at sea, far from any dry land...

dialogues.speaker: Yinxing
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler. I am Yinxing, The Crux's surgeon at sea.

dialogues.speaker: Yinxing
dialogues.text: Whenever a sailor has a health problem, they come to me. I deal with it all — from seasickness and common colds, to amputations, and everything in between.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to learn about treating injuries and illnesses at sea.

dialogues.speaker: Yinxing
dialogues.text: Oh, I presume the Captain arranged this, correct? Alright then, let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Yinxing
dialogues.text: First of all, let me ask you this. What do you think is the biggest danger that all new crew members face?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: That can certainly be a problem at sea, but it's not the biggest danger. The most dangerous thing for a newcomer is to underestimate the dangers of life at sea.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: I have seen many new crew members who see themselves as young and fighting fit and have no regard for safety. They think that since they are tough enough to look after themselves on land, they'll be fine at sea as well.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Those are the ones that always end up in the sick bay. Everyone should know that being a sailor, especially on a long voyage, is a brutal job in an unforgiving environment.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: We have to face malnutrition when we're short on supplies, all kinds of injuries and diseases that the harsh ocean weather can bring...

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: ...and even the psychological problems that can arise due to isolation and the lack of entertainment.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: To make things worse, the lack of medication and treatment options at sea can result in even minor health problems becoming serious, or even fatal...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hence, the need for amputations...?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Haha, you probably thought I was joking, right? That's not surprising. Most newcomers think the same way.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: But hopefully you now realize that with a little extra precaution, a lot of these things can be avoided...

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Well, I think that's enough for you to think over for now.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Is there anything else you would like to know?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Captain Beidou?... Out of everyone I have met, she probably values people's lives and safety the most.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Although I'm just a doctor, Beidou has given me the full authority to send any newcomers who I don't see as fit for service off the ship until they are ready to come back with the right attitude.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Every time we're stocking up before a voyage, medicine takes top priority. I'm even allowed to choose the suppliers regardless of the price, we have adequate budget for medical expenses.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Do you know what Mora-Grubber, our bookkeeper, calls this?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: A significant financial risk. Hehe.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: But Beidou knows the importance of having a healthy crew. That's why she has authorized me regardless.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: She places her full trust in me and believes that I can solve these problems... Of course, I have proven her right.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: So, to answer your question, that's how she thinks!

choices.text: What happens to the crew members who have had limbs amputated?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Hmm? Are you concerned about them? No wonder Captain Beidou thinks you are different, there must be more to you than just your strength.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: If you can convince Mora-Grubber to show you the books, you'll see there is a regular fixed cost, titled "Convalescence Payments and Incapacity Support for Injured Crew Members."

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Regardless of the fleet's income, those who have fought alongside us will certainly receive their compensation every year.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Some of those that have returned to land have started small businesses, while others have chosen to go out traveling the world.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: The money is intended to allow them to live their lives as freely as possible. I'm sure being based on land helps a lot with that, too...

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: Still, we can't pretend like it solves everything. They call them life-changing injuries for a reason, you know?

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: But if nothing else, it's good to know that while Captain Beidou is in charge of The Crux, no one will get forgotten.

response.speaker: Yinxing
response.text: My pleasure. Okay, let's leave it there, then. Be sure to take good care of your health.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Sorry about earlier, Traveler...

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: We were so caught up on getting you to join the fleet that we didn't notice we were going a little overboard... Good thing the Captain stepped in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's okay. I was hoping to learn a little more about cartography.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Oh! Well, in that case, you have come to the right person. I'm not just blowing smoke, you're looking at the most talented navigator in Liyue Harbor.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: I'll start by introducing some chart-reading essentials for new sailors. Feel free to interrupt if you have any questions.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Let's start with what to look for when you get a set of complicated charts.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: First, you should always look at any indicated shorelines, islands or reefs, water depths, hydrological conditions, and other hazards.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: With these features in mind, you can answer the basic question of "can I chart a safe course through this area."

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Visually, nautical charts are a little unique. Unlike land maps, most charts do not have a fixed scale, which means that it can be hard to precisely determine the exact distance between two points.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: The most advanced nautical charts come with a supplementary chart, which has different colored lines marked on it to indicate distances.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: It's worth mentioning that under my direction, The Crux is using these advanced kinds of charts!

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Some cartographers mark out other points of interest on their charts, usually with their own special symbols. If they don't leave any accompanying notes, they can be very difficult to interpret.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For example, charts inherited from the previous navigator?

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Haha, not only those. We have tattered and torn charts that we've picked up from all over the place.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: To be honest, it can be quite a challenge, even for me. Some of these charts are really old and have symbols that I have never seen before...

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: But if we don't decipher them, we will certainly miss many secrets of the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Fortunately, we have the Captain with us. She managed to find some ancient books on semiotics that I can use to study the charts further.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: I don't think anyone other than our Captain could manage to get these kinds of resources. Old charts and ancient books on semiotics are not the kinds of things that are sold in your average marketplace...

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Oops! I've gotten off-topic, hehe. Well, that just about covers the basics of chart-reading.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you would like to know, Traveler?

choices.text: Do you have experience drafting nautical charts?

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: Drafting charts? That's certainly a more advanced topic. To be honest, I've only attained a smattering of knowledge in that area.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: The charts we are using now are just revised versions of the ones left by the previous navigator.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: So my mapping experiences have been primarily limited to updating our charts to reflect changes in the sea.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: I think you can ask Captain Beidou more about cartography.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: One time, the fleet sailed into an uncharted area by mistake. It wasn't long before we turned the fleet around and returned the way we came out for fear of potential hazards.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: But Captain Beidou still managed to draft a simple chart of the area we sailed through for if and when we explore the area again.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: Incredible, isn't it? I was amazed to see that the Captain could even do cartography.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then why does she need you as a navigator?

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: Because I have the talent, and she doesn't want to let it go to waste. Hehe. She treats the whole crew that way.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: I initially had the same question myself. After all, in many fleets the captain also works as the navigator. I couldn't understand her reasoning at the time, so I asked her.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: She just laughed and told me to wise up, saying that even Rex Lapis never fights alone.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: She wants everyone onboard to master their role, so that The Crux is not floating on her alone.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: That way, if the day ever comes when she's no longer with the fleet, we will still be able to sail onward without her.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: Captain Beidou may seem aloof and even act careless sometimes, but the truth is that she's very considerate of everyone onboard.

response.speaker: Huixing
response.text: My pleasure. A friend of Captain Beidou is a friend of mine!

talks.objective: Learn a thing or two from Xu Liushi

dialogues.speaker: Xu Liushi
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler. Are you here to learn about marine meteorology?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, how did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Xu Liushi
dialogues.text: Haha, in my line of work, I've got to have a pair of sharp eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Xu Liushi
dialogues.text: I saw the captain showing you around the training grounds, and then you went to see Yinxing and Huixing.

dialogues.speaker: Xu Liushi
dialogues.text: So, I figured that she probably wants you to get to know the life of a crew member.

choices.text: You have a real knack for your work.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Hehe! Okay, let's get started. First, I'll introduce you to the basics of meteorology.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Marine meteorology basically means keeping tabs on the weather as well as other ocean phenomena, so things like sea fog, storm surges, waterspouts, and so on...

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: These are all potential threats to safe navigation. Luckily, whatever weather might be coming up, there's always some kind of sign that gives it away in advance.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Take waterspouts for example. They're caused by high-speed rotating winds on the surface of the ocean. They can engulf large ships and do immense damage.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: But, if you know that waterspouts can only form in an environment with high temperature, high humidity, and large clouds, then you can be well-prepared.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: You will be even more alert if you also know that the presence of winds blowing in opposite directions with a significant difference in speed is a direct precursor to the formation of waterspouts.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: And most importantly, if you spot a small white vortex emerging from the clouds, you should immediately notify the crew to steer clear of what's ahead.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: So there you go, those are the warning signs of waterspouts. I am proud to say that, over the years, I haven't let a single one sneak up on my watch.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Well, I'm good at reading the sea, but I'm not as good as the captain when it comes to reading people.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Do you know the small fishing village next to Wangshu Inn? I heard that when Captain was a kid, she worked there fishing with the adults.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Later, she made her way into the harbor, where she struggled to make a living. Heh, managing to survive in an environment like that as a kid is solid proof of the Captain's capabilities.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: If it wasn't for her, I never would have dreamed of taking this job. She gave me confidence and told me I could do it.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: You may not have heard, but I'm best known outside the Crux Fleet for a slightly infamous story involving me, Third-Round Knockout, and a few too many...

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Who would ever have thought that the rookie sailor who fell drunk into the sea and became a laughingstock among their now-former crewmates would then go on to become a lookout for The Crux? But it's the unbelievable truth, haha.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: It proves that having skills alone is not enough. You need someone like the Captain who is a good judge of character.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for your time. I think I've learned all that I need for now.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Find me anytime if you want to know more.

choices.text: Sounds like you have a lot of experience.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: I've gotta confess, I learned almost everything I know from the Captain.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: All the stuff about meteorology that I just told you about... she's the real expert.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Do you know the small fishing village next to Wangshu Inn? I heard that when Captain Beidou was a kid, she worked there, fishing.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: Later, she made her way into the harbor, where she struggled to make a living. Heh, growing up in an environment like that, it's no wonder she knows everything about the sea.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: When I first came onboard, I lived every day wallowing in doubt, wondering if my former career as a sailor was all just a waste.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: But as I gradually learned some new things and became more experienced, I finally realized what makes The Crux so great.

response.speaker: Xu Liushi
response.text: After all, not every fleet has the "Uncrowned Lord of the Ocean" as their leader. I feel lucky just to have joined.

choices.text: Looks like Beidou got the right person for the job.

talks.objective: Head to the fishing village near Wangshu Inn
Take a stroll with Beidou in the fishing village
Go with Beidou to the fishing village for a walk

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: How about this pose?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I can't wait to see how you perform.

dialogues.speaker: Yinxing
dialogues.text: Be sure to take good care of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Huixing
dialogues.text: One day, I will decipher all these symbols.

dialogues.speaker: Xu Liushi
dialogues.text: Find me anytime if you want to know more.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: People used to call this place "Downriver," because the villagers apparently moved here from a place called "Upriver."

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: With them, they brought their knowledge of fishing which had been passed down from generation to generation. I learned a lot from them when I was here.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Now, Upriver is long gone and Downriver is all but deserted. It won't be long before no one even remembers what these places are called.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: About a year or two after I arrived, the village chief fell ill during the winter and passed away.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: During that same period, the harvest was getting worse and the fishermen's catch was getting smaller day by day.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Without the village chief to handle the situation, people began blaming each other. There were even rumors that some families had been overfishing, leaving nothing for the rest of the village to catch.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: But in the end, they all turned on me, saying that they shouldn't have ever taken me in. They said I was bad luck.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: They pointed to how that dog died on the first day I arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Next thing you know, the village chief dies, then all the fish die out.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: They said I was a living curse, and the downfall of the village was all my fault.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I told them that I didn't understand. I'm not a curse, I'm just Beidou.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Then some of the villagers started shouting and drove me out of the village.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: They shouted, "Nandou controls life! Beidou controls death... Beidou controls death!"

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Before then, all I knew about my name was that it had something to do with the stars.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: It wasn't until then that I realized that Beidou was a constellation, and the Alcor, one of its stars, was an omen of death.
